title: The Octopus Who Painted the Reef
text: Ollie the octopus loved colours, but his reef was grey. One morning he found a box of coral paints that had fallen from a boat. "I will paint the reef!" he said. With eight arms, he painted eight things at once: red anemones, golden sand, purple shells and a bright blue door for the moray eel. The fish watched with wide eyes. When the sun set, the reef glowed like a rainbow. "You forgot one spot," smiled the eel, pointing at Ollie. So the fish dipped their fins in paint and covered Ollie in happy dots. Now the reef is the brightest home in the sea, and Ollie is the proudest painter in it.

title: Kids Grow Vegetables on School Rooftops
text: More schools are turning their rooftops into little farms. Students plant vegetables like kailan, spinach and cherry tomatoes in neat rows of planter boxes. Teachers say the gardens help children learn where food comes from. Every week, young gardeners water the plants, pull out weeds and check the leaves for insects. When the vegetables are ready, some schools cook them in the canteen, and others share them with families nearby. Growing food in the city also helps the environment, because the vegetables do not need to travel far in lorries. One student said the best part is simple: "Everything tastes better when you grow it yourself!"
